## Fix-scope verification

The reviewed candidate was an unstaged worktree state, so Git does not retain its complete prior
blob. Patch scope was therefore checked against the exact fix-cycle execution record for session
`019fe9d4-1cbb-76d0-b35e-a540a6568708`, then verified against the current postimage.

That record contains one `apply_patch` call targeting only
`20260810133000-codex-update_atomic-adr068-visual-office-rbac.md`, with exactly three hunks:

1. payload `status: "active"` to `status: "draft"`;
2. unqualified body `Status: APPROVED` / `Version: 1.1.0` to the explicit canonical-v1.0.0 and
   proposed-v1.1.0 three-line separation; and
3. the v1.1.0 Version History row from `active` to `draft`, with its summary qualified as inbound
   pending human/MSP review/L2 and not an approval claim.

The patch removes four lines and adds five, all status/authority wording. An in-memory inverse of
those exact hunks reconstructs preimage SHA-256
`21EF84CAA62B08F408912A9065BA67DA224633BC92578AB2B583F7F4343CC44F`; applying the recorded
postimage yields the independently recomputed current SHA-256 above. The module candidate was not
targeted. No unrelated content delta is present in the recorded fix cycle.
